sens: Affirmation of approval regarding an action performed
Encouragement addressed to someone to praise their faithfulness or obedience
G7530.detail:
1. The word expresses a direct and firm approval: it recognizes that an action is good, just, or well executed. It is a word of confirmation, almost an exclamation. In Luke 19:17, the master exclaims, "Well done!" upon seeing the faithfulness of the servant who has made the talents received profitable.
2. Beyond simple approval, it is an encouragement that values the person. The master does not merely acknowledge: he affirms and rewards. This approval recognizes an effort, faithful obedience, a response to expectations.
G7530.origine: This Greek word comes from a root expressing the notion of good. In ancient Greek (in Aristophanes), it is used alone, without a verb, as an interjection — almost a cry of satisfaction. It is a short and powerful word, which spontaneously arises from one who approves. Latin borrowed it in the form "euge."
G7530.emploi: The word appears only once in the New Testament, in Luke 19:17. Jesus recounts the words of the master who praises his faithful servant. This unique occurrence makes it all the more significant: it shows how God welcomes faithfulness in small things. The context is that of the parable of the minas, where the master's approval is the reward for one who did not bury his talent but made it productive. This word "good" opens the door to greater responsibility: "Take charge of ten cities."
G7530.portee: For the Christian, this word reminds us that God does not remain indifferent to faithfulness. Even in small tasks, in obscurity and without human witnesses, He notices and approves. Hearing "well done" from God is the greatest reward. It encourages seeking not the praise of men, but that of the master, knowing that our faithfulness — even when hidden — is seen and recognized. It is a word of grace that frees from fear and doubt.
